rv.q: One of the great musicals of the last decade was born anew on Sunday

This bold musical adaptation of Frank Wedekind's 1891 play about teenage sexual awakening is a powerhouse of raw emotion and contemporary relevance that should connect strongly with younger audiences.
Spring Awakening is a musical of exceptional power and beauty, a show that succeeds in making the late 19th century feel urgently contemporary.
Spring Awakening, a spiky hothouse bloom, drags not only Wedekind’s play but musical theater itself firmly into the now.

A straight shot of eroticism steamed open last night at the Eugene O’Neill Theater under the innocuous name of “Spring Awakening,” and Broadway, with its often puerile sophistication and its sterile romanticism, may never be the same.
Spring Awakening — the breathtaking discussion of what it means to grow up — will become both a high mark of the season and a landmark musical.
Sheik’s absolutely haunting and often breathtaking score still outshine Sater’s poetic lyrics, and many of these songs clearly stand up to repeated listening.
That you leave the theater humming those songs rather than being devastated by what they mean is precisely what keeps Spring Awakening snowbound.

cn.t: Critics hail this daring rock musical as a thrilling original voice on Broadway, praising its raw sexuality, electrifying performances, and innovative fusion of Wedekind's 19th-century tale with contemporary alt-rock intensity.
